a.name: Unequal AI access
a.description: In the treatment-phase AR-glasses press-release task, only one randomly selected member of each two-person team could use Kimi without restrictions on interaction. This is condition 1 (PDF p. 6, Section 3.2). Table 3 prints the corresponding baseline team count; arm-level people counts are not printed.

a.name: Full AI access
a.description: Both members could use Kimi for the treatment-phase AR-glasses press-release task. This is condition 2 (PDF p. 6, Section 3.2). Table 3 prints the corresponding baseline team count; arm-level people counts are not printed.

a.name: No AI access (earlier common baseline)
a.description: Every team first wrote an electric-bicycle press release without GenAI. This is a repeated baseline phase of the same sample, not a separately randomized arm. The order and product prompt were fixed, so its comparisons with the later AI task are excluded (PDF p. 6, Sections 3.2–3.3; PDF p. 14, Section 5.4).

b.name: Unequal AI access
b.description: Only one randomly selected member of each team could use Kimi during the treatment-phase AR-glasses press-release task. Access and team assignment were randomized (PDF p. 6, Sections 3 and 3.2). Arm-specific people counts are not printed.

b.name: Full AI access
b.description: Both members of each team could use Kimi during the same treatment-phase AR-glasses press-release task (PDF p. 6, Sections 3 and 3.2). Arm-specific people counts are not printed.

b.name: No AI access (earlier common baseline)
b.description: All teams first wrote an electric-bicycle press release without AI. This was the earlier task of the same participants, not a separately randomized arm, and must not be added to the study sample. The analyzed count denotes the common experimental sample, not a separately stated post-exclusion baseline total (PDF p. 6, Sections 3 and 3.1-3.3).
